1.note: Two statements about close_pool and the pool registry; both are true and are improvements.

claims.quote: `close_pool()` (`if self.pool:`) will construct a pool just to close and delete it when none exists
claims.notes: Situation: OPTIONS pool is set and no registry entry exists. Reading self.pool builds and registers a pool when none is registered, and close_pool reads self.pool first, so the claim holds. Nothing promises that teardown avoids construction, so this is an improvement.

claims.quote: The `del self._connection_pools[self.alias]` is unguarded while construction uses `setdefault` to be race-tolerant, and a pool that loses that race is never closed.
claims.notes: The del in close_pool has no guard and the pool property uses setdefault. A losing pool is built with open=False and open() is what starts workers, so the losing pool holds no connections. 'Never closed' is true but no harm is shown, and nothing promises thread-safe teardown.

2.note: Three statements about ensure_timezone and pool closing. One is refuted because no per-checkout ensure_timezone exists.

claims.quote: `ensure_timezone()` closes the whole pool on every `TIME_ZONE`/`USE_TZ` change
claims.notes: ensure_timezone() calls close_pool() first. Its only caller is the setting_changed handler, which calls it for each initialized connection on a TIME_ZONE or USE_TZ change. True, and no promise covers the pool reset, so it is an improvement.

claims.quote: Closing a pool under threads holding checked-out connections is hazardous
claims.notes: An opinion. The fact under it, closing while connections are checked out, is true because close_pool runs without waiting for other threads. psycopg-pool documents that in-use connections stay open until returned and are then closed. The hazard is in-use sessions being closed on return, not a crash shown here. No promise, so improvement.

claims.quote: the per-checkout `ensure_timezone` already cover the need
claims.notes: Premise: a per-checkout ensure_timezone exists. None does. Checkout calls pool.getconn() in get_new_connection and init_connection_state skips _configure_connection whenever a pool is used. The method ensure_timezone is called only from the setting_changed handler and closes the pool, and the configure callback is set at pool construction, not per checkout. Nothing runs per checkout, so the claim is refuted.

3.note: The atomic-block guard claim is refuted; the claim about extra guards is an improvement.

claims.quote: The new `in_atomic_block and closed_in_transaction` check is unreachable for every other backend

known_problems.reason: The claim calls the guard pool-only and says three guards compensate for one early None. Whether that objects to the guard as the fault, or only to its placement, is unclear from the words.

claims.notes: Premise: only the pooled _close sets connection None early. Atomic.__exit__ in transaction.py also sets connection.connection to None after a close inside an outermost atomic block when autocommit is off, on any backend. That leaves in_atomic_block and closed_in_transaction set with connection None, so the base guard is reached on SQLite too with AUTOCOMMIT False. The claim is refuted.
evidence: clone/django/db/transaction.py:303-311 (Atomic.__exit__ finally block sets connection None when autocommit is off)

claims.quote: That deviation also forced new guards in `is_usable()` and `init_connection_state()`.
claims.notes: The pre-change postgresql base.py has no connection-None check in is_usable (bcccea3); the head adds one. init_connection_state gained the not-self.pool test. The pooled _close setting None is what needs these guards. No promise, so improvement.
evidence: git show bcccea3 django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py (no 'self.connection is None' in pre-change is_usable)

4.note: A structure remark about repeated open() calls.

claims.quote: `self.pool.open()` runs on every connect
claims.notes: get_new_connection calls self.pool.open() on each connect. psycopg-pool documents open() as safe to call again on an open pool, and _open returns early when the pool is not closed. The call is a no-op after the first, so this is an improvement only.

5.note: The ensure_role deletion is a problem for GT-v11; the other two statements are improvements.

claims.quote: A method and a free function now share the name `ensure_timezone` with different responsibilities
claims.notes: True: the class method ensure_timezone and the module function ensure_timezone both exist. The claim names the naming collision and does not say the module call bypasses subclass overrides, so it does not identify the GT-v5 cause. Improvement.

claims.quote: `_configure_connection` claims to touch nothing on `self` but reads `self.ops`, `self.timezone_name` and `self.settings_dict` on pool worker threads
claims.notes: The comment says the function must not touch self, and the body reads self.ops, self.timezone_name and self.settings_dict (base.py:369-381). The configure callback is passed to ConnectionPool and runs on psycopg-pool's threads. The claim states no consequence for a user and no promise exists. It is not the GT-v1 mechanism, which is the compose_sql wrapper cursor.

claims.quote: the `ensure_role` method is deleted, silently breaking subclass overrides

known_problems.reason: The claim says the deletion silently breaks subclass overrides, so an override stops running with no error. That is the GT-v11 harm, and the deleted ensure_role method is its cause.

claims.notes: Pre-change init_connection_state called self.ensure_role() (bcccea3 base.py:314), so a subclass override ran. At head there is no DatabaseWrapper.ensure_role, and init_connection_state calls _configure_connection, which calls the module ensure_role with OPTIONS['assume_role'], so the override silently stops running. The saved ruling CL-v-ensure-role-override is related, and this review's words state the same harm.
evidence: git show bcccea3:django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:298,314 (ensure_role method and self.ensure_role() call)

6.note: The psycopg2 mismatch restates the GT-v4 cause; the undocumented constraints are an improvement.

claims.quote: `get_connection_params()` raises `ImproperlyConfigured` for psycopg2, while the new docs say the option "is ignored with psycopg2"

known_problems.reason: The claim names the docs saying the option is ignored and the code raising for psycopg2, and calls the two in conflict. It never says what a user who follows the docs gets.

claims.notes: Premise: docs/ref/databases.txt says the option is ignored with psycopg2, and get_connection_params raises 'Database pooling requires psycopg >= 3' when pool is set on psycopg2. Both hold, so the claim is true. It names the mismatch as the fault but states no user consequence, so it only restates the GT-v4 cause.

claims.quote: The `CONN_MAX_AGE` restriction, health-check interaction, and in-atomic-block close behaviour are undocumented.
claims.notes: The pool section does not mention CONN_MAX_AGE, CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS or atomic close, and the code raises for CONN_MAX_AGE != 0. A gap in the documentation is not a promise that these work, so this is an improvement.

claims.quote: goes stale if `OPTIONS["pool"]` changes
claims.notes: django_test_skips is a cached_property that reads OPTIONS['pool'] once, so it does not update if OPTIONS changes after first access. It affects only the test skip list. No promise, so improvement.

claims.quote: about 15 existing tests were rewritten to use a `no_pool_connection()` helper the author calls a hack
claims.notes: The helper at tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py:24-30 carries the comment 'kind of a hack' and is used in about fifteen pre-existing tests. True. Test scaffolding carries no user-facing promise, so improvement.

anchors.quote: Move pool lifecycle into a dedicated registry (lock, `get`, `pop(alias, None)`) so reading never builds and closing never constructs.

safety.reason: A proposal to restructure the registry; no code exists to inspect and the change was not run.

anchors.quote: so the pool reset can be deleted or moved to test support, and the wrapper can remember which pool it checked out from instead of using `_pool`.

safety.reason: Deleting the pool reset would stop time zone changes from reaching pooled connections, since the configure callback runs only when a connection is opened (postgresql/base.py:228-234, 369-381). The review offers moving it to test support as an alternative, which that concern does not cover. Not run.

anchors.quote: Keep the base contract in `_close()` (don't null the connection there) and the base-class change, and the two extra guards, disappear; otherwise confine the check to a PostgreSQL override.

safety.reason: Changing where the atomic-block guard lives or whether _close nulls the connection alters the path the guard protects; the fix does not say how that path is covered, and it was not run.

anchors.quote: a small connection-source abstraction with direct and pooled implementations would delete each branch and let tests inject a source instead of mutating `OPTIONS`.

safety.reason: A design proposal with no code to inspect; not run.

anchors.quote: Restore the method, pass the connection explicitly, or bind needed values up front with `functools.partial`.

sufficiency.reason: Restoring the method would put back the self.ensure_role() dispatch that the override needs, which covers the reported trigger. Passing the connection explicitly or binding values with functools.partial keeps the module-level call that bypasses the override, so only one of the three options cures it.

safety.reason: The fix does not say where a restored ensure_role would run; inside the pool configure callback it would keep the GT-v1 path through compose_sql. Not run.

anchors.quote: Choose one behaviour, validate in one place at pool construction, and fix the docs.

sufficiency.reason: Choosing one behaviour and fixing the docs makes the documented driver configuration match startup behaviour, which is the GT-v4 obligation. Either choice satisfies it.

safety.reason: Either choice keeps the existing safeguard or makes the documentation match it, and neither removes a check that protects users. No new harmful path was found in the inspected code.
